edges.claim: AGC is a major EUV blank supplier (59% market share by one 2025 report)
Hoya is a major EUV blank supplier (34% market share by one 2025 report, or 75%+ by alternative source)

evidence.title: EUV Mask Blanks Market Size, Share & Growth Forecast 2026-2032
evidence.excerpt: Key players include AGC Inc (59% market share) and Hoya (34% market share), accounting for 93% of global market. However, in High-NA EUV segment, Hoya exceeds 75% by volume, with superior process qualifications.
evidence.summary: Market report giving overall EUV blank market share: AGC 59%, Hoya 34%, combined 93% duopoly. Notes High-NA segment with Hoya 75%+ but no separate High-NA share breakdown provided. Scope: appears to be value-based, all grades combined.
evidence.limitations: Market-report page (SEO characteristics); conflicts with prior graph claims (Hoya 75%+/AGC 20-25%). Segment breakdown not separately quantified. No access to underlying primary sources.

evidence.title: Evidence Rebuild: Market Share Conflict Documentation
evidence.summary: This node contains conflicting market-share claims. Prior graph stated Hoya 75%+/AGC 20-25% (per SemiAnalysis/Yole/Morningstar). Verified fetch of intelmarketresearch 2025 report shows AGC 59%/Hoya 34%. Likely causes: different basis (value vs volume), different scope (commodity vs all-grades), aging of sources. Honest resolution: state both numbers with scope caveat and mark as unresolved.
evidence.limitations: Internal documentation; not a primary source. Inaccessible sources: Hoya IR (404), AGC IR (TLS error), Yole (timeout). Prior analyst claims (SemiAnalysis, Yole) could not be re-verified.

evidence.title: Hoya Expands EUV Photomask Blank Capabilities for High-NA Systems
evidence.excerpt: As of Q1 2025, Hoya is understood to be the only vendor with validated blank products for High-NA EUV systems—critical for logic nodes below 2 nm.
evidence.summary: Blog article on Hoya's High-NA EUV blank expansion. States Hoya as 'only vendor with validated blanks' but without supporting qualification documentation, ASML specs, or foundry statements. Describes importance of stricter standards under High-NA shift.
evidence.limitations: Blog/news aggregator source. Claim of single-source qualification stated without citation to official ASML lists or foundry announcements. ASML High-NA product pages do not name suppliers. Appears to be inference from Hoya announcements rather than documented qualification.

evidence.title: High-NA EUV Mask Blank Qualification Status: Unverified
evidence.summary: Prior graph claimed Hoya 100% exclusive/only qualified supplier for High-NA blanks. Rebuild research found: (1) ASML High-NA pages do not list qualified blank suppliers; (2) no Hoya investor docs or ASML qualification matrix accessed; (3) no customer announcement naming exclusive Hoya sourcing found; (4) imec's March 2026 High-NA demo made no mention of supply constraints or exclusive sourcing. Single-source claim lacks verification. Recommendation: downgrade to 'Hoya reported furthest along; qualification status unconfirmed.'
evidence.limitations: Inaccessible primary sources: Hoya annual report, ASML qualification docs, Intel/Samsung/TSMC supply statements. Without these, the 100% claim cannot be validated. Assessment: plausible but unverified.

evidence.title: ASML TWINSCAN EXE High-NA Lithography Systems
evidence.excerpt: The first High NA EUV lithography system was delivered in December 2023... expect the platform to support high-volume chip manufacturing in 2025–2026.
evidence.summary: ASML product page describing High-NA EUV lithography systems (EXE:5000/5200B). Timeline: first delivery Dec 2023, volume 2025-2026. Technical specs: 0.55 NA, 8 nm printing. Confirms segment emergence but does not address mask blank suppliers or qualification.
evidence.limitations: Silent on mask blank sourcing and supplier qualification. Confirms technical timeline and specs only.
